creed.belief: The only difference between the success you see and where I stand today is time.
creed.practice: Just keep trying to become better everyday. That's all.

entries.title: Completed SSC at Purba Muria High School
entries.note: Secondary School Certificate, Sylhet. The first checkpoint.

entries.title: Completed HSC (Science) at Beanibazar Govt. College
entries.note: Higher Secondary Certificate. Chose science, and the path toward engineering.

entries.title: Started B.Sc. in CSE at Leading University
entries.note: Four years of fundamentals, contests, and late nights begin.

entries.title: Qualified for Google Code Jam
entries.note: Cleared the global qualification round in 2020 (42 pts) and again in 2022 (44 pts).

entries.title: ICPC Asia Dhaka Regional, 51st place
entries.note: Competing among the strongest teams in the region.
entries.learning: Hard problems bend to consistent practice.

entries.title: Champion, LU TechStorm 4 programming contest
entries.note: First place on home ground, with Team Catapult.

entries.title: IEEEXtreme 14.0 & 15.0, the 24-hour global marathons
entries.note: Two years of the worldwide 24-hour algorithm contest (Team LURisingStar, 2020; Team SchrodenBug, 2021). The runway to the 16.0 runner-up finish.

entries.title: ICPC Preliminary, 87th of 1,700+ teams
entries.note: One contest among 300+, one rank worth remembering.

entries.title: ACM Coordinator, Leading University Computer Club
entries.note: Mentored juniors in competitive programming and ran peer-to-peer DSA sessions.
entries.learning: Teaching a thing is the fastest way to truly learn it.

entries.title: Joint General Secretary, LU Sports Club
entries.note: Elected to the sports club executive; organized inter-department tournaments and university sporting events.

entries.title: Co-founded & chaired IEEE Computer Society, LU SB Chapter
entries.note: Co-founded the LU Student Branch Chapter and chaired the 2022–2023 session: organized technical events with industry speakers and grew membership by 20%.

entries.title: Organized LU technical bootcamps (2021–2022)
entries.note: Ran hands-on training for juniors: the LU Research Bootcamp (2021) and the Data Communications and Flutter app-development bootcamps (2022).

entries.title: IEEEXtreme 16.0, runner-up in Bangladesh
entries.note: Global rank 149 with Team LazySquad. 24 hours of non-stop problem solving.

entries.title: Joined LII Lab as Software Engineer
entries.note: Built the OnePTE Flutter app from day one and the Django backend powering AI scoring.
entries.obstacle: Owning a full product stack for the first time, while still finishing my degree.
entries.learning: Ship, observe, improve. Ownership is the fastest teacher.

entries.title: Graduated with a B.Sc. in Computer Science and Engineering
entries.note: GPA 3.6/4.0, and 2,000+ solved problems on the side.

entries.title: IEEE Outstanding Leadership Volunteer Award
entries.note: Recognized by IEEE for the 2022–2023 tenure chairing the Computer Society LU Student Branch Chapter.

entries.title: Champion, National Hackathon 2023 at LU CSE Carnival
entries.note: Building under pressure with Team LU Ovream.

entries.title: OneIELTS development begins
entries.note: A second AI-powered test-prep platform: multi-tenant SaaS with a QTI 3.0 exam engine.

entries.title: Promoted to Senior Software Engineer
entries.note: Led backend engineering across two AI-powered English test-prep platforms: architecture, mentoring, and production releases.
entries.learning: Seniority is responsibility for other people's growth, and code comes second.

entries.title: Closed my chapter at LII Lab
entries.note: After 3.5 years, the OnePTE and OneIELTS platforms, 90+ production releases, and a promotion to Senior along the way.
entries.obstacle: Leaving the place and people where I grew from graduate to senior engineer.
entries.learning: Endings are just soil for the next thing to grow in.

entries.title: Started theainativeengineer
entries.note: Began posting regularly on Instagram, Facebook and YouTube: everything I learn, turned into short explainers for engineers.
entries.learning: A channel is a curriculum in public. Consistency, not virality, is the job.

entries.title: Delivered Sushi Lab, a solo end-to-end build
entries.note: Shipped a production bilingual (FR/EN) ordering and marketing platform for a Japanese restaurant in Chartres, France, on Next.js 16, React 19, server actions, and locale-aware checkout.

entries.title: The trail begins
entries.note: Started logging growth publicly: wins, obstacles, and lessons, one day at a time.
entries.learning: Consistency compounds. The tree only grows if you feed it.

entries.title: Upgraded how theainativeengineer ships
entries.note: I have been posting on theainativeengineer since May 2026: short animated explainers on Instagram, Facebook and YouTube, everything I learn, one system behaviour at a time. This is the upgrade to the delivery: a pipeline that turns one idea into a narrated, animated reel, gated at every step, with one promise behind it: don't explain the system, make you watch it run.
entries.obstacle: Most tech content tells you what to type. Almost nothing shows what actually happens underneath.
entries.learning: Systems intuition is usually earned from outages. It can be compressed.

entries.title: Met Hasanuzzaman Shamim, Technical Lead Software Engineer at Authlab
entries.note: Discussed AI in the tech industry as a whole: how it is changing, how it is affecting us, and how we are coping with it.
entries.learning: Meetups like this exist to widen the picture. Someone else's vantage point is the cheapest upgrade there is.

entries.title: Production infrastructure live for our first product
entries.note: Stood up the production environment for a product I've been building from zero: servers, database, deploy path and readiness checks, all verified end to end.

entries.title: Released our first Google Play app
entries.note: Submitted the first release to Google Play: store listing, screenshots and all. From a blank Flutter project to a shipping app in a few months.
entries.obstacle: Everything that has to be true before a store accepts an app, all at once.
entries.learning: Shipping is a checklist, not a feeling.

entries.title: Talked with Saiful Islam, Senior Engineering Manager at Optimizely
entries.note: Discussed the founder journey, the app business, what a product based company looks like from the inside, the traits of a great product, and how to approach all of it.
entries.learning: Great products come from clear traits and a deliberate approach, not luck.

entries.title: Talked with Ariful Jannat Arif, Principal Software Engineer at Enosis
entries.note: Discussed the traits of good software, the metrics behind it, and the KPIs that matter on Google Play and the App Store.
entries.learning: What you measure on the store is what the store rewards. Know the KPIs before you ship.
